title: Insulin in hospital: targets, regimens, hypoglycaemia, discharge

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the ADA Standards of Care, diabetes care in the hospital. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: What is the glucose target range for most hospitalised patients?
questions.why: Tighter targets increased hypoglycaemia and mortality in intensive care trials. A range of 110 to 140 is acceptable for selected patients if it can be reached safely.

questions.q: Why is sliding-scale insulin alone discouraged for hospitalised patients with diabetes?
questions.a: It treats hyperglycaemia after the fact and never prevents it
d: It is only licensed for type 1 diabetes
questions.why: A scheduled basal dose, with correction added on top, gives better control with no more hypoglycaemia. Correction-only regimens are the commonest inpatient error.

questions.q: A non-critically ill patient with type 2 diabetes is eating normally. Which insulin regimen is preferred?
questions.why: When intake is poor or unpredictable the prandial doses are dropped and basal plus correction is used instead.

questions.q: What total daily insulin dose is a usual starting point for an insulin-naive hospitalised patient?
questions.why: About half is given as basal and half divided across meals. Older patients and those with kidney impairment start at 0.2 to 0.3 units per kg.

questions.q: A patient on basal-bolus insulin is made nil by mouth for a procedure. What happens to the insulin?
questions.a: Continue basal, usually at a reduced dose, and hold the prandial doses
questions.why: Basal insulin covers the liver's glucose output whether or not the patient eats. Stopping it, especially in type 1 diabetes, invites ketoacidosis.

questions.q: Below what glucose is hypoglycaemia defined in hospital?
questions.why: Under 54 is clinically significant, level 2, and any episode with altered mental status is level 3 regardless of the number.

questions.q: A conscious patient who can swallow has a glucose of 62 mg/dL. What is the first treatment?
questions.a: 15 grams of fast carbohydrate, then recheck in 15 minutes
questions.why: Intravenous dextrose is for patients who cannot swallow safely, and glucagon for those without intravenous access. The insulin regimen is then reduced, not abandoned.

questions.q: A patient started on prednisone 40 mg each morning has glucose readings that climb through the afternoon and settle overnight. Which insulin adjustment fits that pattern?
questions.a: A morning dose of NPH insulin
d: An evening dose of long-acting insulin
questions.why: Once-daily morning steroids raise glucose from midday to evening; NPH given with the steroid peaks in the same window and wears off overnight.

questions.q: Which oral class is generally not recommended for use during a hospital admission?
questions.why: The concern is euglycaemic ketoacidosis in patients who are acutely ill, fasting or perioperative. DPP-4 inhibitors are the one oral class with reasonable inpatient data.

questions.q: When should metformin be held in hospital?
questions.a: Around iodinated contrast, and with acute kidney injury, sepsis or hypoxia
d: Only if the patient is nil by mouth
Never; it is safe in all inpatients
questions.why: The risk is lactic acidosis when the drug accumulates. It restarts once kidney function is stable, typically 48 hours after contrast.

questions.q: A patient admitted on metformin alone has an admission A1c of 11%. What should the discharge regimen include?
questions.a: Basal insulin added to the metformin
d: Metformin alone at a higher dose
No change; recheck A1c in 3 months
questions.why: An admission A1c under 7 means resume the home regimen; 7 to 9 means intensify; above 10 usually means discharge on insulin, with a follow-up within a month.

questions.q: The evening before surgery, what fraction of a patient's usual long-acting basal insulin should be given?
questions.why: Short-acting insulin is held while fasting. Continuous glucose monitoring or hourly checks cover the gap in the operating room.
